Human: Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic physics and test contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0
- Bird(double startY) begins at y=startY and vy=0.0; applyGravity() performs vy=clamp(vy+0.5,-10.0,10.0), integrate() performs y+=vy, and flap() replaces vy with -8.0 rather than adding -8.0 to the old velocity
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed,400.0,600.0,100), begins RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0, and contains zero pipes until the documented spawn interval elapses
- one running tick must call Bird.applyGravity() and then Bird.integrate(); collision must be tested on the resulting unclamped position, so Game.tick must not clamp the bird back inside the world before CollisionDetector.hitBounds can report a terminal boundary hit
- Game uses the exact public methods boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), and java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(); do not alternate between Bird-returning snapshots, void tick, flap, or other aliases
- RNG must store the constructor seed in a final long originalSeed field; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming or changing java.util.Random state, while nextDouble() and nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to the stored java.util.Random
- Game's RNG field is private RNG rng without final because reset(long seed) must assign rng=new RNG(seed); the delegating constructor must initialize final configuration fields and call reset(seed), and must not first assign a final RNG that reset then tries to reassign
- ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) is the independently testable scoring rule: it returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX and calls pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes
- MainTest contains exactly 2--4 short deterministic tests and never indexes an initially empty pipe list; use ScoreSystem with a handcrafted PipePair for scoring instead of waiting for a spawn
- the exact physics fixture is: new Game(12345L) has birdY 300.0 and birdVy 0.0; one tick yields birdVy 0.5 and birdY 300.5; after reset(12345L), flap yields -8.0, then one tick yields birdVy -7.5 and birdY 292.5
- the exact RNG fixture creates RNG a and RNG b with seed 98765L, calls a.seed() twice before any random draw, then compares a.nextDouble() with b.nextDouble() and a.nextInt(100) with b.nextInt(100); never consume a random value from only one instance and later claim the streams are at the same position, and never assert two successive random values must differ
- the exact scoring fixture creates PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0): passedPipe(149.0,pipe) and passedPipe(150.0,pipe) are false because the trailing edge is 150.0 and the comparison is strict; passedPipe(151.0,pipe) is true and marks scored; a later passedPipe(160.0,pipe) is false
- use exact collision signatures hitBounds(Bird bird,double birdHeight,double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird,double birdWidth,double birdHeight,PipePair pipe,double worldHeight); top-pipe vertical overlap is bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0, while bottom overlap is bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(); never compare a y coordinate with pipe.x()
- Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird,30.0,worldHeight) alone, then iterates for (PipePair pipe : pipes) and calls hitPipe(bird,30.0,30.0,pipe,worldHeight) on that one pipe; passing pipes, a List<PipePair>, to the single-PipePair parameter is forbidden and no list overload may be invented
- tick count starts at zero; each successful tick increments ticks exactly once and only then spawns when ticks % spawnInterval == 0, so the default game remains pipe-free for ticks 0 through 99 and first spawns on completed tick 100
- Main must call game.tick() as a standalone statement and ignore its boolean result before printing getters; it must never embed game.tick() in concatenation, formatting, assignment, or any value expression
- assertions and messages must agree with screen coordinates: downward motion means a larger y and upward motion means a smaller y; never assert that gravity makes y smaller or velocity more negative
- repeat the exact Game API, mutable Game RNG field/reset construction, coordinate convention, numeric constants, replacement flap, tick order, per-pipe collision loop and formulas, non-consuming RNG seed and paired-stream fixture, empty initial pipe list and tick-100 spawn, strict-boundary scoring fixture, standalone Main tick call, and exact physics fixture in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic physics and test contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0
- Bird(double startY) begins at y=startY and vy=0.0; applyGravity() performs vy=clamp(vy+0.5,-10.0,10.0), integrate() performs y+=vy, and flap() replaces vy with -8.0 rather than adding -8.0 to the old velocity
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed,400.0,600.0,100), begins RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0, and contains zero pipes until the documented spawn interval elapses
- one running tick must call Bird.applyGravity() and then Bird.integrate(); collision must be tested on the resulting unclamped position, so Game.tick must not clamp the bird back inside the world before CollisionDetector.hitBounds can report a terminal boundary hit
- Game uses the exact public methods boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), and java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(); do not alternate between Bird-returning snapshots, void tick, flap, or other aliases
- RNG must store the constructor seed in a final long originalSeed field; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming or changing java.util.Random state, while nextDouble() and nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to the stored java.util.Random
- Game's RNG field is private RNG rng without final because reset(long seed) must assign rng=new RNG(seed); the delegating constructor must initialize final configuration fields and call reset(seed), and must not first assign a final RNG that reset then tries to reassign
- ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) is the independently testable scoring rule: it returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX and calls pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes
- MainTest contains exactly 2--4 short deterministic tests and never indexes an initially empty pipe list; use ScoreSystem with a handcrafted PipePair for scoring instead of waiting for a spawn
- the exact physics fixture is: new Game(12345L) has birdY 300.0 and birdVy 0.0; one tick yields birdVy 0.5 and birdY 300.5; after reset(12345L), flap yields -8.0, then one tick yields birdVy -7.5 and birdY 292.5
- the exact RNG fixture creates RNG a and RNG b with seed 98765L, calls a.seed() twice before any random draw, then compares a.nextDouble() with b.nextDouble() and a.nextInt(100) with b.nextInt(100); never consume a random value from only one instance and later claim the streams are at the same position, and never assert two successive random values must differ
- the exact scoring fixture creates PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0): passedPipe(149.0,pipe) and passedPipe(150.0,pipe) are false because the trailing edge is 150.0 and the comparison is strict; passedPipe(151.0,pipe) is true and marks scored; a later passedPipe(160.0,pipe) is false
- use exact collision signatures hitBounds(Bird bird,double birdHeight,double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird,double birdWidth,double birdHeight,PipePair pipe,double worldHeight); top-pipe vertical overlap is bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0, while bottom overlap is bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(); never compare a y coordinate with pipe.x()
- Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird,30.0,worldHeight) alone, then iterates for (PipePair pipe : pipes) and calls hitPipe(bird,30.0,30.0,pipe,worldHeight) on that one pipe; passing pipes, a List<PipePair>, to the single-PipePair parameter is forbidden and no list overload may be invented
- tick count starts at zero; each successful tick increments ticks exactly once and only then spawns when ticks % spawnInterval == 0, so the default game remains pipe-free for ticks 0 through 99 and first spawns on completed tick 100
- Main must call game.tick() as a standalone statement and ignore its boolean result before printing getters; it must never embed game.tick() in concatenation, formatting, assignment, or any value expression
- assertions and messages must agree with screen coordinates: downward motion means a larger y and upward motion means a smaller y; never assert that gravity makes y smaller or velocity more negative
- repeat the exact Game API, mutable Game RNG field/reset construction, coordinate convention, numeric constants, replacement flap, tick order, per-pipe collision loop and formulas, non-consuming RNG seed and paired-stream fixture, empty initial pipe list and tick-100 spawn, strict-boundary scoring fixture, standalone Main tick call, and exact physics fixture in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). {"Implementation approach":"Architect Bob designs a minimal, deterministic Java 11 Maven repository for a headless Flappy Bird core. Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.

Full API specification (repeated):
- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].
- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.
- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.
- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.
- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).
- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.
- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.
- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.

Logic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):
- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.
- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.
- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.
- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.
- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.

Test Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):
- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.
- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. Tests never index the initial empty pipes list and do not wait for spawn.

Shared Knowledge (repeated rules in tasks):
- Maintain coordinate convention and numeric constants: gravity=+0.5, flap=-8.0, speed clamp=[-10.0,10.0], bird size 30x30, world size 400x600, spawnInterval=100, birdX constant used by Game for scoring and collision.
- Tick order, collision calls signatures and per-pipe loop, RNG contract with non-consuming seed, mutable Game.rng replaced by reset, strict scoring before off-screen removal, first spawn after completed tick 100.

Roles:
- Alice: physics and collisions (Bird.java, CollisionDetector.java).
- Eve: randomness and obstacles (RNG.java, PipePair.java).

The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.

Full API specification (repeated):
- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].
- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.
- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.
- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.
- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).
- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.
- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). - Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.

- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.

The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.\\n- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.\\n\\nLogic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.\\n- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.\\n- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.\\n- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.\\n- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.\\n- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.\\n- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.\\n\\nLogic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.\\n- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.\\n- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.\\n- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.\\n- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.\\n- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.\\n- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.\\n- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.\\n- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.\\n- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.\\n- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.\\n- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.\\n\\nLogic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.\\n- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.\\n- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.\\n- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.\\n- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.\\n- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.\\n\\nFull API specification (repeated):\\n- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].\\n- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.\\n- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.\\n- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.\\n- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.\\n- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).\\n- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.\\n- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.\\n- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.\\n\\nLogic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.\\n- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.\\n- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.\\n- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.\\n- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.\\n\\nTest Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):\\n- Provide exactly 2–4 short deterministic JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java/MainTest.java.\\n- Tests cover: physics fixture (Game(12345L) initial state; after one tick vy=0.5, y=300.5); reset and flap fixture (after reset(12345L), flapBird(), then one tick vy=-7.5, y=292.5); RNG paired stream fixture with seed 98765L; scoring fixture using handcrafted PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0) verifying strict trailing-edge comparison. Tests never index the initial empty pipes list and do not wait for spawn.\\n\\nShared Knowledge (repeated rules in tasks):\\n- Maintain coordinate convention and numeric constants: gravity=+0.5, flap=-8.0, speed clamp=[-10.0,10.0], bird size 30x30, world size 400x600, spawnInterval=100, birdX constant used by Game for scoring and collision.\\n- Tick order, collision calls signatures and per-pipe loop, RNG contract with non-consuming seed, mutable Game.rng replaced by reset, strict scoring before off-screen removal, first spawn after completed tick 100.\\n\\nRoles:\\n- Alice: physics Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic physics and test contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0
- Bird(double startY) begins at y=startY and vy=0.0; applyGravity() performs vy=clamp(vy+0.5,-10.0,10.0), integrate() performs y+=vy, and flap() replaces vy with -8.0 rather than adding -8.0 to the old velocity
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed,400.0,600.0,100), begins RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0, and contains zero pipes until the documented spawn interval elapses
- one running tick must call Bird.applyGravity() and then Bird.integrate(); collision must be tested on the resulting unclamped position, so Game.tick must not clamp the bird back inside the world before CollisionDetector.hitBounds can report a terminal boundary hit
- Game uses the exact public methods boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), and java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(); do not alternate between Bird-returning snapshots, void tick, flap, or other aliases

- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0

{"Implementation approach":"Architect Bob designs a minimal, deterministic Java 11 Maven repository for a headless Flappy Bird core. Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.

Full API specification (repeated):
- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].
- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.
- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.
- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.
- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).
- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.
- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.
- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.

Logic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):
- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.
- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.
- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.
- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.
- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.

Test Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):

Generate a complete medium-size Java 11 repository architecture for: Flappy bird game.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: pom.xml
- runtime entry: src/main/java/Main.java
- single test target: src/test/java/MainTest.java
- test command: mvn -q test
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use Maven and Java 11 without preview features. Main.java must be in the default package because the evaluator runs Main. Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. This deliberately avoids package/import mismatches in independently generated files. Keep core logic independent from Swing/JavaFX; prefer no GUI and no non-test external dependency. pom.xml MUST declare org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter with test scope and a Maven Surefire version that runs JUnit 5; MainTest.java must use JUnit Jupiter only. Repeat this exact dependency contract in the pom.xml task.


Project-specific Java deterministic physics and test contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0
- Bird(double startY) begins at y=startY and vy=0.0; applyGravity() performs vy=clamp(vy+0.5,-10.0,10.0), integrate() performs y+=vy, and flap() replaces vy with -8.0 rather than adding -8.0 to the old velocity
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed,400.0,600.0,100), begins RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0, and contains zero pipes until the documented spawn interval elapses
- one running tick must call Bird.applyGravity() and then Bird.integrate(); collision must be tested on the resulting unclamped position, so Game.tick must not clamp the bird back inside the world before CollisionDetector.hitBounds can report a terminal boundary hit
- Game uses the exact public methods boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), and java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(); do not alternate between Bird-returning snapshots, void tick, flap, or other aliases
- RNG must store the constructor seed in a final long originalSeed field; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming or changing java.util.Random state, while nextDouble() and nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to the stored java.util.Random
- Game's RNG field is private RNG rng without final because reset(long seed) must assign rng=new RNG(seed); the delegating constructor must initialize final configuration fields and call reset(seed), and must not first assign a final RNG that reset then tries to reassign
- ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) is the independently testable scoring rule: it returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX and calls pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes
- MainTest contains exactly 2--4 short deterministic tests and never indexes an initially empty pipe list; use ScoreSystem with a handcrafted PipePair for scoring instead of waiting for a spawn
- the exact physics fixture is: new Game(12345L) has birdY 300.0 and birdVy 0.0; one tick yields birdVy 0.5 and birdY 300.5; after reset(12345L), flap yields -8.0, then one tick yields birdVy -7.5 and birdY 292.5
- the exact RNG fixture creates RNG a and RNG b with seed 98765L, calls a.seed() twice before any random draw, then compares a.nextDouble() with b.nextDouble() and a.nextInt(100) with b.nextInt(100); never consume a random value from only one instance and later claim the streams are at the same position, and never assert two successive random values must differ
- the exact scoring fixture creates PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0): passedPipe(149.0,pipe) and passedPipe(150.0,pipe) are false because the trailing edge is 150.0 and the comparison is strict; passedPipe(151.0,pipe) is true and marks scored; a later passedPipe(160.0,pipe) is false
- use exact collision signatures hitBounds(Bird bird,double birdHeight,double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird,double birdWidth,double birdHeight,PipePair pipe,double worldHeight); top-pipe vertical overlap is bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0, while bottom overlap is bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(); never compare a y coordinate with pipe.x()
- Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird,30.0,worldHeight) alone, then iterates for (PipePair pipe : pipes) and calls hitPipe(bird,30.0,30.0,pipe,worldHeight) on that one pipe; passing pipes, a List<PipePair>, to the single-PipePair parameter is forbidden and no list overload may be invented
- tick count starts at zero; each successful tick increments ticks exactly once and only then spawns when ticks % spawnInterval == 0, so the default game remains pipe-free for ticks 0 through 99 and first spawns on completed tick 100
- Main must call game.tick() as a standalone statement and ignore its boolean result before printing getters; it must never embed game.tick() in concatenation, formatting, assignment, or any value expression
- assertions and messages must agree with screen coordinates: downward motion means a larger y and upward motion means a smaller y; never assert that gravity makes y smaller or velocity more negative
- repeat the exact Game API, mutable Game RNG field/reset construction, coordinate convention, numeric constants, replacement flap, tick order, per-pipe collision loop and formulas, non-consuming RNG seed and paired-stream fixture, empty initial pipe list and tick-100 spawn, strict-boundary scoring fixture, standalone Main tick call, and exact physics fixture in Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Test Scope Plan, Shared Knowledge, and every affected implementation task


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 8 repository files
- about 35 functions or methods
- about 700 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- bird position and flap physics
- gravity and deterministic ticks
- pipe movement and gaps
- collision rules
- score updates when pipes pass
- game-over and reset

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents

{"Implementation approach":"Architect Bob designs a minimal, deterministic Java 11 Maven repository for a headless Flappy Bird core. Protocol-required files are preserved exactly: pom.xml, src/main/java/Main.java, and a single test at src/test/java/MainTest.java. All classes are in the default package with no package declarations and live directly under src/main/java. The runtime entry Main.java remains thin: it constructs Game, performs one standalone game.tick() call (ignoring its boolean result), then prints getters (birdY, birdVy, ticks, score, pipe count). The core domain is split into concrete files: Bird (physics), RNG (seeded randomness), PipePair (obstacles), CollisionDetector (pure collision rules), ScoreSystem (pure scoring rule), Game (orchestration). There is no GUI, no frameworks, and no external dependencies beyond JUnit Jupiter for tests. Physics, RNG, scoring, tick order, spawn timing, and Main invocation strictly follow the provided fixtures.

Full API specification (repeated):
- Coordinates: x increases rightward; y increases downward. Gravity is +0.5 per tick; flap sets vy to -8.0; clamp velocity to [-10.0,10.0].
- Bird(double startY): y=startY, vy=0.0; applyGravity(): vy=clamp(vy+0.5, -10.0, 10.0); integrate(): y+=vy; flap(): replace vy with -8.0.
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed, 400.0, 600.0, 100); starts RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0 and vy=0.0; pipes list initially empty until spawn at completed tick 100.
- Tick order: one running tick calls Bird.applyGravity() then Bird.integrate(); collision is tested on resulting unclamped position. Game.tick first calls hitBounds(bird, 30.0, worldHeight), then per pipe calls hitPipe(bird, 30.0, 30.0, pipe, worldHeight). Tick increments ticks exactly once; spawn occurs when ticks % spawnInterval == 0 (first spawn on completed tick 100). Game must not clamp the bird before CollisionDetector reports bounds hit.
- Game API: boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(). No aliases.
- RNG: stores constructor seed in final long originalSeed; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming RNG; nextDouble()/nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to stored java.util.Random; Game has private RNG rng (mutable by reset).
- Scoring: ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX; marks pipe scored via pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes.
- Collision: hitBounds(Bird bird, double birdHeight, double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird, double birdWidth, double birdHeight, PipePair pipe, double worldHeight). Top overlap: bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0. Bottom overlap: bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(). Never compare any y with pipe.x(). Game.tick calls these exact signatures per the described order.
- Main: must call game.tick() as a standalone statement, ignore its boolean result, then print getters; no embedding in any value expression.

Logic Analysis (repeated fixtures enforcement):
- Gravity increases vy by +0.5 (downward) and y increases after integrate() when vy>0. Flap overwrites vy=-8.0 regardless of previous value; clamp is applied in applyGravity only.
- Tick sequence correctness ensures physics applied before collision detection; no clamping is allowed before collision checks. Bound collision uses unclamped y and y+birdHeight.
- Spawn timing: ticks start at 0; after each successful tick increment ticks once; a pipe is spawned when ticks % 100 == 0; default game has no pipes for ticks 0..99; first spawn occurs on completed tick 100.
- Scoring strictness: ScoreSystem triggers only when trailing edge (pipe.x()+pipe.width()) is strictly less than birdX; only once per pipe via markScored; Game increments score based on this check before any off-screen removal.
- RNG paired streams: seed() is non-consuming; calling a.seed() multiple times does not move the random stream; paired instances produce same nextDouble and nextInt(bound) if their consumption is identical.

Test Scope Plan (repeated fixtures enforcement):

Put every other project class directly under src/main/java and keep it in the default package too; do not create package subdirectories or package declarations. Project-specific Java deterministic physics and test contract:
- use screen coordinates consistently: x increases rightward and y increases downward; gravity is exactly +0.5 per tick, an upward flap velocity is exactly -8.0, and maximum speed magnitude is 10.0
- Bird(double startY) begins at y=startY and vy=0.0; applyGravity() performs vy=clamp(vy+0.5,-10.0,10.0), integrate() performs y+=vy, and flap() replaces vy with -8.0 rather than adding -8.0 to the old velocity
- Game(long seed) delegates to Game(seed,400.0,600.0,100), begins RUNNING with bird y=worldHeight/2.0, and contains zero pipes until the documented spawn interval elapses
- one running tick must call Bird.applyGravity() and then Bird.integrate(); collision must be tested on the resulting unclamped position, so Game.tick must not clamp the bird back inside the world before CollisionDetector.hitBounds can report a terminal boundary hit
- Game uses the exact public methods boolean tick(), void reset(long seed), void flapBird(), double birdY(), double birdVy(), long ticks(), int score(), and java.util.List<PipePair> pipes(); do not alternate between Bird-returning snapshots, void tick, flap, or other aliases
- RNG must store the constructor seed in a final long originalSeed field; seed() returns originalSeed without consuming or changing java.util.Random state, while nextDouble() and nextInt(int bound) delegate directly to the stored java.util.Random
- Game's RNG field is private RNG rng without final because reset(long seed) must assign rng=new RNG(seed); the delegating constructor must initialize final configuration fields and call reset(seed), and must not first assign a final RNG that reset then tries to reassign
- ScoreSystem.passedPipe(double birdX, PipePair pipe) is the independently testable scoring rule: it returns true exactly once when pipe.x()+pipe.width()<birdX and calls pipe.markScored(); Game checks scoring before removing off-screen pipes
- MainTest contains exactly 2--4 short deterministic tests and never indexes an initially empty pipe list; use ScoreSystem with a handcrafted PipePair for scoring instead of waiting for a spawn
- the exact physics fixture is: new Game(12345L) has birdY 300.0 and birdVy 0.0; one tick yields birdVy 0.5 and birdY 300.5; after reset(12345L), flap yields -8.0, then one tick yields birdVy -7.5 and birdY 292.5
- the exact RNG fixture creates RNG a and RNG b with seed 98765L, calls a.seed() twice before any random draw, then compares a.nextDouble() with b.nextDouble() and a.nextInt(100) with b.nextInt(100); never consume a random value from only one instance and later claim the streams are at the same position, and never assert two successive random values must differ
- the exact scoring fixture creates PipePair(100.0,50.0,100.0,150.0,3.0): passedPipe(149.0,pipe) and passedPipe(150.0,pipe) are false because the trailing edge is 150.0 and the comparison is strict; passedPipe(151.0,pipe) is true and marks scored; a later passedPipe(160.0,pipe) is false
- use exact collision signatures hitBounds(Bird bird,double birdHeight,double worldHeight) and hitPipe(Bird bird,double birdWidth,double birdHeight,PipePair pipe,double worldHeight); top-pipe vertical overlap is bird.y()<pipe.gapY() && bird.y()+birdHeight>0.0, while bottom overlap is bird.y()<worldHeight && bird.y()+birdHeight>pipe.gapY()+pipe.gapHeight(); never compare a y coordinate with pipe.x()

- tick count starts at zero; each successful tick increments ticks exactly once and only then spawns when ticks % spawnInterval == 0, so the default game remains pipe-free for ticks 0 through 99 and first spawns on completed tick 100
- Main must call game.tick() as a standalone statement and ignore its boolean result before printing getters; it must never embed game.tick() in concatenation, formatting, assignment, or any value expression
- assertions and messages must agree with screen coordinates: downward motion means a larger y and upward motion means a smaller y; never assert that gravity makes y smaller or velocity more negative
